name: Selling Numbers
description: Boris really likes numbers and even owns a small shop selling interesting numbers. He has n decimal numbers B i . Cost of the number in his shop is equal to the sum of costs of its digits. You are given the values c d , where c d is the cost of the digit d . Of course, Boris is interested in that numbers he owns have the maximum cost possible. Recently Boris got hold of the magical artifact A , which can allow him to increase the cost of his collection. Artifact is a string, consisting of digits and ' ? ' symbols. To use the artifact, Boris must replace all ' ? ' with digits to get a decimal number without leading zeros (it is also not allowed to get number 0). After that, the resulting number is added to all numbers B i in Boris' collection. He uses the artifact exactly once. What is the maximum cost of the collection Boris can achieve after using the artifact?
input_specification: First line contains artifact A , consisting of digits ' 0 '–' 9 ' and ' ? ' symbols ( 1 ≤ | A | ≤ 1000 ). Next line contains n — the amount of numbers in Boris' collection ( 1 ≤ n ≤ 1000 ). Next n lines contain integers B i ( 1 ≤ B i < 10 1000 ). A doesn't start with ' 0 '. Last line contains ten integers — costs of digits c 0 , c 1 , ..., c 9 ( 0 ≤ c i ≤ 1000 ).
output_specification: Output one integer — the maximum possible cost of the collection after using the artifact.
approach_summary: Express count as f(R) - f(L-1). Define memoized state dp[pos][tight][leading_zeros][cond] scanning digits from most to least significant in O(digits × base × states).

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 778E — Selling Numbers [439. Digit DP]
topic_editorial.summary: Digit DP counting values in range $[L, R]$.
topic_editorial.key_invariant: Counting valid integers in range $[L, R]$ can be decomposed into $f(R) - f(L-1)$, where $f(X)$ counts valid integers in $[0, X]$. Numbers $\le X$ can be formed digit-by-digit from the most significant position. The constraint that the prefix does not exceed $X$ is tracked by a single boolean flag `tight`.
